items.stem: Explain why tan A can take any positive value but sin A cannot exceed 1.
items.answer: tan A = opp/adj can be any positive ratio; sin A = opp/hyp and the hypotenuse is the longest side.
items.markingKey: Key points: tan A = opp/adj can be any positive ratio; sin A = opp/hyp and the hypotenuse is the longest side. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem:

Reason (R): Right triangles with the same acute angle are similar.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.

items.stem: In △ABC right-angled at B, AB = 12 cm and BC = 5 cm. Find AC and cot A.
items.answer: AC = 13 cm; cot A = 12/5
items.markingKey: AC² = 12² + 5² = 169 ⇒ AC = 13. For angle A, BC is opposite and AB adjacent: cot A = adjacent/opposite = 12/5.

items.stem: If tan A = 21/20, where A is acute, find cosec A and sin A.
items.answer: cosec A = 29/21, sin A = 21/29
items.markingKey: Take a right triangle with opposite side 21k, adjacent side 20k, hypotenuse 29k (Pythagoras). Then cosec A = 29/21, sin A = 21/29 (3 marks).

items.stem: If tan θ = 21/20, evaluate sin²θ + cos²θ.
items.markingKey: From tan θ = 21/20, take sides opposite 21, adjacent 20, hypotenuse 29: sin θ = 21/29, cos θ = 20/29, tan θ = 21/20. Substitute: 1 (3 marks).

items.stem: A ramp for wheelchairs at a school entrance rises 80 m over a horizontal distance of 18 m. Let θ be the angle the ramp makes with the ground. (i) Find the length of the ramp. (ii) Find sin θ. (iii) Find cos θ. (iv) Find tan θ and say what it represents.
items.answer: (i) 82 m (ii) 40/41 (iii) 9/41 (iv) 40/9, the rise per metre of horizontal run (steepness)
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.answer: (i) 5 m (ii) 3/5 (iii) 4/5 (iv) 3/4, the rise per metre of horizontal run (steepness)

items.stem: Explain why the trigonometric ratios of angle A depend only on A and not on the size of the right triangle.
items.answer: All right triangles with acute angle A are similar (AA), so the side ratios are the same.
items.markingKey: Key points: All right triangles with acute angle A are similar (AA), so the side ratios are the same. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: Explain how knowing one trigonometric ratio of an acute angle determines all the others.
items.answer: One ratio fixes two sides in proportion; Pythagoras gives the third; then all ratios follow.
items.markingKey: Key points: One ratio fixes two sides in proportion; Pythagoras gives the third; then all ratios follow. Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: A kite flies at the end of a straight string. The angle θ of the string with the ground satisfies tan θ = 24/7. The horizontal distance from the child to the point below the kite is 35 m. (i) Find the height of the kite. (ii) Find sin θ and cos θ. (iii) Find the length of the string. (iv) Express sec θ in terms of tan θ and check its value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: If cot θ = 8/15, evaluate (1 + tan²θ).
items.markingKey: From cot θ = 8/15, take sides opposite 15, adjacent 8, hypotenuse 17: sin θ = 15/17, cos θ = 8/17, tan θ = 15/8. Substitute: 289/64 (3 marks).

items.stem: In a quiz, a team is told that for an acute angle θ, sin θ = 20/29. (i) Find cos θ using an identity. (ii) Find tan θ. (iii) Verify 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ. (iv) Find sec θ + tan θ and sec θ − tan θ, and their product.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Or by Pythagoras on the triangle.

items.stem: Evaluate (5 cos²60° + 4 sec²30° − tan²45°)/(sin²30° + cos²30°).
In △ABC right-angled at B, AB = 4 cm and BC = 3 cm. Find AC and sin A.
items.answer: AC = 5 cm; sin A = 3/5
items.markingKey: AC² = 4² + 3² = 25 ⇒ AC = 5. For angle A, BC is opposite and AB adjacent: sin A = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/5.

items.stem: Given tan A = 7/24, A acute, find the other five trigonometric ratios of A.
items.answer: sin A = 7/25, cos A = 24/25, cosec A = 25/7, sec A = 25/24, cot A = 24/7
items.markingKey: Take sides opposite 7k, adjacent 24k; hypotenuse 25k by Pythagoras. Then sin A = 7/25, cos A = 24/25, cosec A = 25/7, sec A = 25/24, cot A = 24/7.

items.stem: Express cosec A and cot A in terms of cos A.
items.answer: cosec A = 1/√(1 − cos²A); cot A = cos A/√(1 − cos²A).
items.markingKey: Key points: cosec A = 1/√(1 − cos²A); cot A = cos A/√(1 − cos²A). Award 2 marks for a complete, correctly reasoned answer.

items.stem: Prove that (cosec A − sin A)(sec A − cos A) = 1/(tan A + cot A).
items.answer: Proof
items.markingKey: LHS = (cos²A/sin A)(sin²A/cos A) = sin A cos A; RHS = 1/(1/(sin A cos A)) = sin A cos A. (Marks: correct identity used, simplification, conclusion.)

items.stem: Prove that √((1 + sin A)/(1 − sin A)) = sec A + tan A.
items.answer: Proof
items.markingKey: Multiply inside by (1 + sin A)/(1 + sin A): √((1 + sin A)²/cos²A) = (1 + sin A)/cos A. (Marks: correct identity used, simplification, conclusion.)
